title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page 4 of an English typescript, almost certainly a preprint of Dennis Sullivan's 'Differential forms and the topology of manifolds' (Manifolds–Tokyo 1973, publ. 1975), which ended up in this folder. The section title, the notation Λ(x1,x2,…;d) → {smooth forms}, the tower of nilmanifolds starting from the Jacobian, and the Hodge-theoretic rigidification of the model all match that paper.

The mathematics, step by step:

(1) End of the previous section. For a manifold M, the minimal model gives a map φ: M → H/Γ to a compact nilmanifold. This map generalises to a tower of maps M → N_k. The N_k are the nilmanifolds attached to the Malcev completions of the lower-central-series quotients of π1(M), equivalently to the degree-1 part of the minimal model filtered by stages. The tower begins with the Albanese/Jacobian torus H_1(M,R)/H_1(M,Z). This is the de Rham-theoretic analogue of the Albanese map and its nilpotent higher analogues (cf. Chen's iterated integrals, later Hain).

(2) Riemannian case.
- Hodge decomposition: Ω = im d ⊕ im d* ⊕ Harm. Each form decomposes uniquely as ω = dx_ω + d*y_ω + h_ω, with x_ω ∈ im d*, y_ω ∈ im d, h_ω harmonic.
- Formal input ('disjointness' of d and d*): ⟨dd*x, x⟩ = |d*x|², so dd*x = 0 ⇒ d*x = 0; dually d*dy = 0 ⇒ dy = 0.
- Hence ω is closed iff y_ω = 0. Indeed dω = dd*y; if this vanishes then d*y = 0. Writing y = dz gives d*dz = 0, so dz = y = 0.
- A closed ω is cohomologous to its canonical harmonic representative h_ω.
- An exact ω equals d of the canonical primitive x_ω = d*Gω.

(3) Purpose. The construction of the model map ρ: Λ(x_i; d) → Ω*(M) requires choices: representatives of cohomology classes for the generators, and primitives for the forms that must be killed. Using harmonic representatives and the canonical primitives d*G makes ρ canonical. This is Sullivan's 'Riemannian model'. The page breaks off at 'we have to choose'.

Context in the folder. The folder concerns ½-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes, divided powers Γ^n, exterior powers and multiplicative structures. The preprint was presumably consulted for commutative cochain models and rational homotopy (Sullivan models). Nothing on this page is written by Grothendieck.
errors: d* = *d* is correct only up to sign: on p-forms in dimension n, d* = (−1)^{n(p+1)+1} *d*. The typescript drops the sign, which is standard informal usage.
The Jacobian should be H_1(M,R)/(image of H_1(M,Z)), i.e. H_1(M,Z) modulo torsion. A harmless abuse.

'Follows on the formal level' hides the analytic input: the existence of the decomposition (ellipticity, the Green operator) on a compact manifold. Only the uniqueness and the closed/exact characterisations are formal.

ideas.what: Tower of maps from M to nilmanifolds (Malcev completions of the lower central series quotients of π1), starting with the Albanese/Jacobian torus
ideas.modern_name: Higher Albanese manifolds / nilpotent Albanese tower from the 1-minimal model
ideas.where_published: Sullivan, 'Differential forms and the topology of manifolds' (1975); 'Infinitesimal computations in topology' (1977)

ideas.what: Hodge decomposition with uniqueness via the 'disjointness' of d and d*; harmonic representatives and canonical primitives
Using Hodge theory to make the Sullivan model map ρ: Λ(x_i;d) → Ω*(M) canonical for a Riemannian manifold

missed.claim: Archival/historical point: a typescript of Sullivan's differential-forms paper is filed inside Grothendieck's 1975–76 notes on ½-simplicial complexes, divided powers and multiplicative structures. This documents that Grothendieck was reading Sullivan's rational homotopy theory (commutative DGA models) while working on multiplicative structures on complexes. It is a small datum about the reception of rational homotopy theory by Grothendieck, years before Pursuing Stacks. It is not a mathematical result.
missed.quote: We can use the Hodge decomposition to rigidify the model of a Riemannian manifold.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild interest to historians tracing Grothendieck's contacts with homotopy theory (Sullivan, Quillen) in the mid-1970s. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript of Sullivan's published paper, not Grothendieck's work. The mathematics is standard and well credited. The only interest is archival: the preprint sits in Grothendieck's folder on multiplicative structures.
transcription_corrections: The page is an English typescript, not Grothendieck's handwriting. It is apparently D. Sullivan's 'Differential forms and the topology of manifolds'.
The isolated 'ρ' line belongs to the sentence 'In the construction of ρ: Λ(x_1, x_2, …; d) → {smooth forms}'.
The handwritten '4' at the lower left is an archival page number.
